title: Cursors That Draw, Glass in Layers, Invented Hands, Intent & Scroll-Built Lightbox
description: Five patterns about arrival: work you watch happen rather than find already finished.

drops.title: The Page Builds Itself
drops.description: A flock of cursors draws a landing page back onto a blank plate, box by box and letter by letter.
drops.concept: The page is stored as a blueprint of rects, text layers and rules rather than markup, and each cursor runs one task to completion — dragging a box out with a live size badge, typing copy behind an I-beam, pulling a rule across. Tasks unlock top-down so a card's title waits for its card, and when nothing is left the swarm flocks to your pointer with simple separation steering.
drops.source: DhvanilPatel/swarm-cursors, itself a tribute to Joel Califa's Swarm

interaction.mouse: Move anywhere — once the build finishes the cursors chase your pointer and spread apart as they crowd
interaction.click: Pick 1×/2×/3× build speed, set the swarm size from 2 to 8, toggle the ruler guides, or replay the whole build
interaction.touch: Drag to lead the flock; the panel docks to the bottom on narrow screens

drops.title: Glass, Taken Apart
drops.description: Six switches build one liquid-glass surface — and the ink reads the wallpaper behind it and flips.
drops.concept: The material is assembled in order: shadow, a lifted and saturated backdrop, a refracting rim that samples a wider crop so content bends inward, dispersion that sends red further than blue, tint, then rim light top-left and bottom-right. Each surface samples fifteen points of the wallpaper behind it and switches to dark glass with light text when the average falls below half.

interaction.mouse: Drag any of the three panes over different parts of the wallpaper and watch the ink decide for itself
interaction.click: Switch any layer off to see what it was doing, tune blur, rim width, bend and tint, swap wallpapers, or copy the CSS
interaction.touch: Panes drag with a finger; the panel moves to the bottom-right on small screens

drops.title: Hands That Never Existed
drops.description: Letters as single-line skeletons, inked by a nib that thickens on the downstroke — three hands at once.
drops.concept: There is no font file: every glyph is a short list of arcs and lines on an x-height grid, and the pen walks that skeleton at a set speed, widening as it travels downward and laying ink at partial alpha so crossings darken on their own. A seed gives each hand its own slant, wobble and joining strokes, and a correction is struck through rather than erased.

interaction.mouse: Nothing to hover — the writing is the page; the sliders retune the pen between runs
interaction.click: Type your own sentence and press Write it, or hit Make a mistake to watch the second hand strike a word out and carry on
interaction.touch: Sheets stack vertically and the pen panel sits inline under them

drops.title: Interactivity Arrives on Intent
drops.description: Zero behaviour at boot: the module is fetched while your pointer is still moving toward the control.
drops.concept: One delegated listener per event type covers the whole page, and each control only names an action it has never loaded. Pointer-enter, focus or touch-start starts the import; the click then finds it warm and runs in a fraction of a millisecond. Flip the policy to visible, idle or none and the timeline shows exactly what each click had to pay for.

interaction.mouse: Hover a control and watch its module load before you arrive; the dot turns green when it is armed
interaction.click: Switch preload policy, raise the simulated latency, or forget every module and start the page inert again
interaction.touch: touchstart counts as intent, so the first tap still warms the module before the click resolves

drops.title: A Lightbox Built From Scrolling
drops.description: The thumbnail morphs into the slide, the carousel is a scroll-snap strip, and a pull downward lets it go.
drops.concept: Opening hands one view-transition-name from the thumbnail to the slide inside the DOM update, so only one element ever wears it and the browser morphs between them. Slides live in an ordinary horizontal scroller with snap points, so swiping is native scrolling with native momentum, and a vertical drag is captured separately to scale and fade the slide away.

interaction.mouse: Click a plate to morph it open, wheel to move between slides, double-click to zoom and drag to pan, ctrl + wheel zooms at the pointer
interaction.click: Toggle the morph, snapping and elastic pull, or move the dismiss threshold; arrows navigate and Escape closes
interaction.touch: Swipe is plain scrolling; drag the slide downward past the threshold to dismiss it back into its tile
